name: unflick-mcp

tools.name: play
tools.description: Play a video file or URL. URLs from supported streaming sites (YouTube, Bilibili, Twitch, Vimeo, etc.) are extracted via the bundled yt-dlp before playback.

file.description: Path to a local video file, or HTTP(S) URL to a streaming site.

proxy.description: Optional proxy URL forwarded to yt-dlp for URL extraction (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:7890)

tools.name: pause
tools.description: Pause playback. Acts on the player the user is watching — when the unflick window is open, this pauses the video on screen.

tools.name: resume
tools.description: Resume playback after a pause. From end-of-file this rewinds to the start rather than doing nothing.

tools.name: stop
tools.description: Stop playback and unload the file. The resume point is saved unless the file was watched to the end.

tools.name: seek
tools.description: Seek to a position in seconds

tools.name: set_volume
tools.description: Set volume level

tools.name: set_speed
tools.description: Get or set the playback speed of the window the user is watching. Call with no arguments to read the current rate. Pitch is corrected by default, so speech stays natural — see the `pitch` CLI command to turn that off.

rate.description: Speed multiplier between 0.01 and 100 (e.g. 1.5). Omit to read the current rate.

relative.description: Treat `rate` as an offset from the current speed instead of an absolute multiplier. Clamped to the valid range.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Get current playback status including state, file, position, duration, volume, and speed. `file` is the path the user gave; `key` is what resume points and bookmarks are filed under (the same string, except for a mounted disc, where it identifies the disc rather than the drive) and `label` is a disc's volume name.

tools.name: file_info
tools.description: Get media file metadata (duration, resolution, codecs) without affecting current playback

file.description: Path to the media file

tools.name: playlist_add
tools.description: Add a file to the playlist

file.description: Path to the media file

tools.name: playlist_remove
tools.description: Remove a playlist entry by index

index.description: Index of the entry to remove

tools.name: playlist_list
tools.description: List all playlist entries with index, path, and current track indicator

tools.name: playlist_next
tools.description: Advance to and play the next track in the playlist

tools.name: playlist_prev
tools.description: Go back to and play the previous track in the playlist

tools.name: playlist_clear
tools.description: Clear all entries from the playlist

tools.name: playlist_play
tools.description: Play a specific playlist entry by index

index.description: Index of the playlist entry to play

tools.name: load_subtitle
tools.description: Load an external subtitle file

file.description: Path to the subtitle file (.srt, .ass, .sub)

tools.name: subtitle_list
tools.description: List all subtitle tracks (embedded and external)

tools.name: subtitle_select
tools.description: Select a subtitle track by ID (0 to disable subtitles). Choosing a single track turns bilingual mode off.

tools.name: audio_list
tools.description: List all audio tracks (embedded)

tools.name: audio_select
tools.description: Select an audio track by ID (0 to disable audio)

tools.name: generate_subtitles
tools.description: Generate subtitles for a video using whisper. Mode 'local' uses bundled or supplied whisper.cpp; mode 'api' uses OpenAI. Returns the path of the generated .srt file.

mode.description: Transcription mode (auto-detected from arguments if omitted)

model.description: Path to whisper model (local mode; auto-detects bundled if omitted)

whisper.description: Path to whisper-cli (local mode; auto-detects bundled if omitted)

tools.name: translate_subtitles
tools.description: Translate an SRT file to another language using OpenAI. Returns the path of the translated .srt file.

tools.name: library_scan
tools.description: Scan a directory for video files and add them to the library

tools.name: library_search
tools.description: Search the media library by title or path

tools.name: library_list
tools.description: List all media files in the library

tools.name: library_remove
tools.description: Remove a media entry from the library by ID

tools.name: clip
tools.description: Extract a video clip segment, optionally as GIF. Requires ffmpeg in PATH.

file.description: Input file path (uses currently playing file if omitted)

gif.description: Export as GIF instead of MP4

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Take a screenshot of the current video frame

output.description: Output file path (optional, auto-generated if omitted)

tools.name: save_position
tools.description: Save playback position for a file (for resume playback)

tools.name: get_position
tools.description: Get saved playback position for a file

tools.name: settings_path
tools.description: Get the absolute path of the settings.json file

tools.name: settings_get
tools.description: Read all settings, or a single key if provided

key.description: Optional key name; omit to read all settings

tools.name: settings_set
tools.description: Set a single settings key to the given JSON value

value.description: Any JSON value (string, number, bool, object, array)

tools.name: settings_unset
tools.description: Remove a single settings key

tools.name: filter_list
tools.description: List current video filter values (brightness, contrast, saturation, gamma, hue)

tools.name: filter_set
tools.description: Set a video filter (brightness | contrast | saturation | gamma | hue) to a value in -100..100

tools.name: filter_reset
tools.description: Reset all video filters to 0 (neutral)

tools.name: sponsor_segments
tools.description: Fetch SponsorBlock skip segments for a YouTube URL. Returns the configured categories plus a list of {start, end, category, action_type, uuid} segments. Empty list when none exist (404). Errors only on network/parse failure or non-YouTube URLs.

tools.name: subtitle_delay
tools.description: Get or set the subtitle delay in seconds. Positive values show subtitles later. Call with no arguments to read the current delay. Useful for correcting AI-generated subtitles, which often drift a few hundred milliseconds from the dialogue.

relative.description: Treat `seconds` as an offset from the current delay instead of an absolute value

seconds.description: Delay in seconds. Omit to read the current value.

tools.name: audio_delay
tools.description: Get or set the audio delay in seconds, for fixing lip-sync. Positive values play audio later. Call with no arguments to read the current delay.

relative.description: Treat `seconds` as an offset from the current delay instead of an absolute value

seconds.description: Delay in seconds. Omit to read the current value.

tools.name: subtitle_style_get
tools.description: Read subtitle appearance: scale, vertical position, colour, border size, bold.

tools.name: subtitle_style_set
tools.description: Set one subtitle appearance property. Returns the full style after the change.

value.description: scale: 0.1-10 · pos: 0-150 (100 = bottom) · color: #RRGGBBAA · border_size: 0-20 · bold: boolean

tools.name: subtitle_bilingual
tools.description: Show two subtitle tracks at once — typically the original plus a translation. Call with no arguments to read the current state. `primary` is the bottom line and the one `subtitle_select` refers to; `secondary` is drawn just above it. Each accepts a track id from subtitle_list or a path to a subtitle file, which is loaded if it is not already. With no tracks named, the original and the translation are picked automatically. Selecting a single track with subtitle_select turns this off.

enabled.description: Turn it on or off. Omit to read; omitting it while naming a track or layout turns it on.

layout.description: stacked (just above the first line, the default) or top of the frame

primary.description: Bottom line: a track id, or a path to a subtitle file

secondary.description: The line above it: a track id, or a path to a subtitle file

tools.name: chapter_list
tools.description: List the chapters of the currently playing file: index, title, start time, and which one is playing. Returns an empty list for files without chapters.

tools.name: chapter_seek
tools.description: Jump to a chapter by 0-based index.

tools.name: chapter_next
tools.description: Jump to the next chapter. Clamps at the last chapter.

tools.name: chapter_prev
tools.description: Jump to the previous chapter. Clamps at the first chapter.

tools.name: ab_loop
tools.description: Control the A-B loop, which repeats a section of the current file. Set point A and point B to start looping; clear to stop. Omit `position` to use the current playback position.

action.description: a/b set a loop bound, clear removes both, status reads them

position.description: Position in seconds for the a/b actions. Defaults to the current position.

tools.name: frame_step
tools.description: Step forward exactly one frame. Pauses playback, as frame stepping is for inspecting a still.

tools.name: frame_back_step
tools.description: Step back exactly one frame. Pauses playback.

tools.name: playlist_repeat
tools.description: Get or set the playlist repeat mode. 'off' stops after the last entry, 'one' loops the current file, 'all' wraps around. Call with no arguments to read the current mode.

tools.name: playlist_shuffle
tools.description: Get or set playlist shuffle. Enabling it reorders playback without renumbering entries, and keeps the current track playing. Call with no arguments to read the current setting.

tools.name: shutdown
tools.description: Shut down the unflick daemon. Declined when the control port is held by the GUI — close the window instead.

tools.name: get_subtitles
tools.description: Find and load subtitles for the playing video from OpenSubtitles, in one step. Picks the best match: a subtitle synced against this exact file if one exists (checked by file hash, so the timing is correct), otherwise the most-downloaded subtitle for the title. Prefer this over generate_subtitles when the video is a released film or show — a human-made subtitle is more accurate and arrives in a second rather than minutes. Requires the user's own OpenSubtitles API key in the `opensubtitles_api_key` setting; it fails with instructions if unset. Costs one of the user's limited daily downloads, so do not call it repeatedly.

file.description: Video to match against. Defaults to the playing file.

languages.description: Comma-separated OpenSubtitles language codes, e.g. "zh-CN,en". Defaults to the opensubtitles_languages setting, else English.

load.description: Load the subtitle into the player after downloading (default true)

query.description: Search text. Omit to derive a title from the playing file's name.

tools.name: find_subtitles
tools.description: Search OpenSubtitles and return the candidates without downloading anything. Use this when the user should choose, or to check what exists before spending a download. Each result carries a file_id for download_subtitle, plus `moviehash_match` — true means it is synced to this exact file. Costs no download quota. Requires the user's own OpenSubtitles API key in the `opensubtitles_api_key` setting.

file.description: Video to match against. Defaults to the playing file.

hash.description: Match by file hash as well as title (default true). Set false to search by title only.

query.description: Search text. Omit to derive a title from the playing file's name.

tools.name: download_subtitle
tools.description: Download one subtitle chosen from find_subtitles and load it into the player. Saved next to the video when that directory is writable, so it loads automatically next time. Costs one of the user's limited daily OpenSubtitles downloads.

file.description: Video to save the subtitle beside. Defaults to the playing file.

file_id.description: The file_id from a find_subtitles result

language.description: Language code of the chosen subtitle, used in the saved filename

load.description: Load it into the player after downloading (default true)

tools.name: search_transcript
tools.description: Search the currently playing file's subtitles for a phrase and return every match with its timestamp and speaker (if known). Works with loaded subtitle files, sidecar .srt/.vtt/.ass/.ssa files, embedded text tracks, and subtitles you generated with generate_subtitles. Use this to answer questions about what is said in a video, or to find the moment to jump to. Case-insensitive substring match, not regex.

file.description: Optional path to a video or subtitle file; defaults to the playing file

tools.name: seek_to_text
tools.description: Jump playback to where a phrase is spoken. Finds the phrase in the subtitles (optionally filtered by speaker) and seeks just before that line, so the sentence is heard from its start. This is the 'skip to the part where they talk about X' tool.

file.description: Optional path to a video or subtitle file; defaults to the playing file

tools.name: transcript_get
tools.description: Return the full transcript of the currently playing file as timed cues (including speaker labels when present), plus where it came from. Use it to read or summarise a video, or as input for writing your own chapter list with set_chapters. Long videos produce a lot of text — prefer search_transcript or transcript_summary when you only need a passage or overview.

file.description: Optional path to a video or subtitle file; defaults to the playing file

tools.name: transcript_summary
tools.description: Return a compact, structured overview of a video's transcript: cue count, word count, speaking duration, top keywords, and timeline segments with representative lead lines. Much smaller than transcript_get on a long video, so reach for this first when asked what a video is about or how it is structured.

file.description: Optional path to a video or subtitle file; defaults to the playing file

segments.description: Number of timeline segments to divide the transcript into (1-20, default 5)

tools.name: library_transcript_search
tools.description: Search spoken dialogue across every video in the media library that has a sidecar (.srt/.vtt) or cached transcript. Returns each matching cue with its video path, title, and timestamp so you can immediately open that video at that line with `play` (passing `file` and `seek`).

query.description: Phrase to search for across the library (case-insensitive)

tools.name: generate_chapters
tools.description: Give a file that has no chapters a set of them, derived from the pauses in its transcript. The result becomes real navigation: it shows up in chapter_list, marks the progress bar, and responds to chapter_seek. This is a rough heuristic — if you have read the transcript, set_chapters will give better titles and boundaries.

count.description: Roughly how many chapters to aim for (2-50, default 8)

tools.name: set_chapters
tools.description: Set the chapter list for a file that has none, from your own reading of its content. Times are in seconds; they are sorted and clamped to the file automatically. These become real chapters — navigable with chapter_seek and drawn on the progress bar. Fails if the file already ships with its own chapters.

tools.name: clear_chapters
tools.description: Remove chapters added by generate_chapters or set_chapters. A file's own built-in chapters are not affected.

tools.name: keybind_list
tools.description: List every keyboard shortcut: action id, label, current key, default, and whether the user has changed it. Keys read as Mod+Alt+Shift+key, where Mod is Ctrl on Windows/Linux and Cmd on macOS.

tools.name: keybind_set
tools.description: Rebind a keyboard shortcut. Fails if the key is already taken by another action, naming the conflict rather than silently stealing it.

action.description: Action id from keybind_list, e.g. play_pause

key.description: Key, e.g. k · Shift+z · Mod+o · PageUp

tools.name: keybind_reset
tools.description: Restore a shortcut to its default. Omit `action` to reset every binding at once.

action.description: Action id. Omit to reset all.

tools.name: video_transform_get
tools.description: Read how the picture is fitted to the window: aspect override, rotation, zoom multiplier, pan-scan and deinterlace. Distinct from filter_list, which is colour rather than geometry.

tools.name: video_transform_set
tools.description: Fix a squashed aspect ratio, straighten a video recorded sideways, crop black bars, or deinterlace broadcast footage.

value.description: aspect: "auto" | "16:9" | 1.78 · rotate: 0|90|180|270 · zoom: multiplier, 1 = fit · panscan: 0-1 · deinterlace: boolean

tools.name: video_transform_reset
tools.description: Restore the file's own geometry — no aspect override, no rotation, no zoom or pan-scan, deinterlace off.

tools.name: incognito
tools.description: Read or set incognito mode. While on, nothing is written to the play history — including plays started from the CLI or by you. Call with no arguments to read it.

tools.name: recent_files
tools.description: Recently played files, newest first, with how many times each was played and when. Covers files opened directly, not just ones scanned into the library.

tools.name: recent_clear
tools.description: Forget the play history. Scanned library metadata is kept — only the played-at times and counts are cleared.

tools.name: bookmark_add
tools.description: Save a named position in a file, so it can be jumped back to later. Defaults to where playback is right now in the file the user is watching. Bookmarks persist across sessions and are recorded even in incognito mode, since they are asked for explicitly.

file.description: Path or URL. Defaults to what's playing.

name.description: Label for the spot. Omit and it shows as its timestamp.

position.description: Seconds into the file. Defaults to the current position; required when bookmarking a file that isn't playing.

tools.name: bookmark_list
tools.description: Bookmarks for the file being watched, in timeline order. Pass all=true for every file, or file to ask about a specific one. Each entry carries the id that bookmark_goto takes, and the `key` it is filed under — the path for a file, the disc's own identity for a disc.

all.description: Every file instead of just one.

file.description: Path or URL. Defaults to what's playing. A drive path resolves to the disc currently in it.

key.description: Exactly this identity, unresolved — from disc_list, get_status, or the `key` on a listed bookmark. Use it to reach bookmarks left under a drive letter before discs had an identity.

tools.name: bookmark_goto
tools.description: Jump to a bookmark by id. Seeks if its file is already playing; otherwise opens that file at the bookmarked position, saving a resume point for the outgoing one. A bookmark on a disc is refused, without loading anything, when that disc is not the one in the drive.

tools.name: bookmark_rename
tools.description: Give a bookmark a name, or drop the one it has by omitting name.

name.description: New label. Omit to remove the name.

tools.name: bookmark_remove
tools.description: Delete one bookmark by id.

tools.name: bookmark_clear
tools.description: Delete every bookmark for the file being watched, or for the file named. Pass all=true to delete them for every file — that scope is never reached by default.

file.description: Path or URL. Defaults to what's playing. A drive path resolves to the disc currently in it.

key.description: Exactly this identity, unresolved — from disc_list, get_status, or the `key` on a listed bookmark. This is how bookmarks orphaned under a drive letter are deleted.

tools.name: mouse_list
tools.description: List mouse bindings: wheel up/down, click, double click, middle click, and the four right-drag gestures, each with the action it runs.

tools.name: mouse_set
tools.description: Point a mouse trigger at an action. Unlike keys, two triggers may share an action — wheel-up and drag-up both raising volume is fine, since the inputs are distinct. Pass "none" as the action to disable a trigger.

trigger.description: Trigger id from mouse_list, e.g. wheel_up, gesture_left

tools.name: mouse_reset
tools.description: Restore a mouse trigger to its default. Omit `trigger` to reset all of them.

tools.name: script_list
tools.description: List installed mpv user scripts (.lua and .js) in the config scripts folder, with each script's path, language, description, and whether it is enabled.

tools.name: script_add
tools.description: Install a .lua or .js mpv user script into the config scripts directory, enable it, and load it into the running player immediately.

path.description: Path to the .lua or .js script file to install

tools.name: script_toggle
tools.description: Enable or disable an installed mpv user script by filename (e.g. "autocrop.lua") or stem ("autocrop"). Enabling loads the script immediately; disabling takes effect on the next launch.

enabled.description: True to enable, false to disable

tools.name: script_remove
tools.description: Delete an installed mpv user script from the config scripts directory.

name.description: Script filename or stem to remove

tools.name: describe_frame
tools.description: Return the frame showing right now as an image, so you can see what is on screen. Optionally seek to a position first. The picture is the one the viewer is watching — GUI, CLI and MCP share a single player. Downscaled to keep the response small; subtitles and on-screen controls are not burned in.

tools.name: transcript_speakers
tools.description: List all speakers in the transcript with cue count, word count, speaking duration, and first/last timestamp. Pass `detect: true` to run lightweight acoustic + conversational turn diarization when subtitles do not already carry speaker labels.

count.description: Target number of speakers when detect=true (2-8)

detect.description: Run automatic speaker diarization if true (default false)

file.description: Optional path to a video or subtitle file; defaults to the playing file

tools.name: transcript_rename_speaker
tools.description: Rename a speaker label across the transcript (e.g. from "Speaker 1" to "Host" or "Alice"). The rename is persisted in cache so subsequent transcript_get, search_transcript, and transcript_summary calls reflect it.

file.description: Optional path to a video or subtitle file; defaults to the playing file

tools.name: transcript_export
tools.description: Export the transcript to a formatted string or file in `txt`, `srt`, `vtt`, or `json` format, optionally filtered to a single speaker.

file.description: Optional path to a video or subtitle file; defaults to the playing file

output.description: Optional output file path. Omit to receive the formatted text in the response.

tools.name: frame_contact_sheet
tools.description: Sample a grid of frames (cols × rows) evenly across a time range of the video and return a single tiled JPEG image plus the exact timestamp of every cell. Ideal for surveying what visually happens across a video or section in one multimodal tool call instead of calling describe_frame a dozen times.

end.description: End time in seconds (default: file duration)

file.description: Optional video file path; defaults to the playing file

max_edge.description: Target sheet width in pixels (256-2048, default 1280)

tools.name: detect_scenes
tools.description: Detect visual scene cuts / shot boundaries in the video using ffmpeg's scene-change filter. Useful for videos without dialogue or transcripts (screen recordings, silent footage, music videos). Set `to_chapters: true` to immediately install the detected scenes as navigable chapters on the playing file.

file.description: Optional video file path; defaults to the playing file

max_scenes.description: Maximum number of scenes to return (1-100, default 20)

threshold.description: Scene change sensitivity threshold between 0.05 and 0.95 (default 0.3; lower detects more subtle cuts)

to_chapters.description: Apply detected scenes as virtual chapters on the playing file

tools.name: playlist_save
tools.description: Save the current playlist to an `.m3u`, `.m3u8`, or `.pls` file.

tools.name: playlist_load
tools.description: Load an `.m3u`, `.m3u8`, or `.pls` playlist file into the player's queue. Relative paths inside the playlist are resolved against the playlist file's directory.

append.description: Append to the existing playlist instead of replacing it (default false)

path.description: Path to the .m3u, .m3u8, or .pls playlist file

tools.name: equalizer_get
tools.description: Read the 10-band equaliser: per-band gains in dB, the band centre frequencies they correspond to, the preamp, whether loudness normalisation is on, and the filter chain mpv is actually running. Read this before changing a band so you adjust the user's curve instead of replacing it.

tools.name: equalizer_set
tools.description: Adjust the equaliser. Set one band with `band` (0-9, low to high) plus `gain` in dB, or the whole curve at once with `bands`. `enabled` switches the equaliser in and out without discarding the curve, `normalize` evens out quiet dialogue against loud action, and `preamp` makes headroom so boosted bands don't clip. Gains are clamped to ±12 dB. Every change rebuilds mpv's audio filter chain, so set a whole curve in one call rather than nine.

bands.description: All ten gains in dB, low frequency first

enabled.description: Switch the equaliser on or off, keeping the curve

gain.description: Gain in dB for that band, -12 to 12

tools.name: equalizer_preset
tools.description: Apply a named equaliser curve and switch the equaliser on. Use equalizer_presets to see what exists and what each is for. 'speech' lifts dialogue out of a loud mix and 'night' tames explosions while keeping voices — those two answer most requests about not being able to hear what people are saying.

name.description: Preset name, e.g. speech, night, bass, treble, headphones, flat

tools.name: equalizer_presets
tools.description: List the available equaliser presets with a description of what each is for and the curve it applies.

tools.name: equalizer_reset
tools.description: Remove every audio filter: flat curve, no preamp, no normalisation.

tools.name: pitch_correction
tools.description: Read or set whether changing playback speed keeps the original pitch. On by default, which is what makes 1.5x speech listenable rather than chipmunk-like. Turn it off only when the pitch shift is the point, such as checking a musical tempo change.

enabled.description: Omit to read the current setting

tools.name: window_mode
tools.description: Get or set the shape of the player window the user is looking at. `normal` is the full player, `pip` is a small always-on-top video window, `music` is the compact audio layout with cover art and tags. Call with no arguments to read the current mode. Only works while the unflick GUI is running — the headless daemon has no window and says so.

mode.description: Mode to switch to. Omit to read the current one.

tools.name: cleanup
tools.description: Find files an older unflick left behind — on Windows, upgrading from v0.9 moved the install directory and stranded roughly half a gigabyte with no uninstall entry. Reports by default; pass `apply` to delete. The live thumbnail and cover caches share that folder and are never touched.

apply.description: Delete what was found. Omit to report only.

tools.name: cast
tools.description: Send what is playing to a television on the network over DLNA. "list" finds renderers; "to" starts a cast (naming a renderer, or omitting it when there is only one) and pauses playback here so it is not heard twice; "stop", "pause", "resume", "seek" and "status" drive it once it is running. Only local files can be cast — the television fetches them from this machine.

file.description: A file to cast instead of what is playing.

renderer.description: Which renderer, by name or part of it. Omit when there is only one.

seconds.description: For seek, where to go. For list and to, how long to wait for renderers to answer (default 3).

tools.name: disc_list
tools.description: Optical drives on this machine and whether each holds a DVD or Blu-ray, plus whether this build can play them at all. Play one with `play` and the drive path ("D:\\"), a disc image ("film.iso"), or a folder holding VIDEO_TS / BDMV; a specific title is mpv's own syntax, "dvd://3". Each drive, and each probed path, also reports `key` — the identity its bookmarks and resume point are filed under, which changes when the disc does — and `label`, the volume name.

path.description: Ask about one path instead of listing drives — reports what it is without opening it.

tools.name: session
tools.description: What the user was last watching and how far in — and, with action "restore", reopen it there. unflick writes this down every few seconds while playing, so it survives a closed window or a crash. Use it when someone asks to get back to what they were watching without naming the file. "clear" forgets it.

action.description: Defaults to show, which only reports.

tools.name: startup
tools.description: The last launch's startup timeline, phase by phase, in milliseconds from process start — process init, video pipeline, window shown, the launch file opening, React mounting, the control port. Use it to say where a slow start went rather than that it was slow.

tools.name: now_playing
tools.description: What is playing, described the way a person would: title, artist, album, and whether there is any picture (an embedded cover is not video). Use this rather than `get_status` when the question is 'what is this', and `get_status` when it is 'where are we'.

cover.description: Also extract the embedded cover art and return its path on disk. Costs one ffmpeg run the first time per file.

tools.name: dev_snapshot
tools.description: The accessibility tree of the unflick window: every visible element with its role, accessible name, state and a CSS selector that feeds straight back into dev_click and dev_text. Reach for this first — it is how you find out what is on screen. Invisible nodes and unnamed wrappers are elided, so what comes back is what a person would see. Needs the GUI running, started with --allow-dev.

selector.description: Scope to a subtree instead of the whole document.

tools.name: dev_click
tools.description: Click an element in the unflick window. Polls for the selector first, so a click issued right after an action does not race the render, then hit-tests the point before dispatching: if something else is on top, the click is refused and the covering element is named rather than reported as a success. A selector matching several elements is refused unless `index` says which.

index.description: Which match, 0-based, when the selector is ambiguous.

selector.description: CSS selector. Take it from dev_snapshot.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for the selector to appear. Default 5.

tools.name: dev_text
tools.description: Visible text of every element matching a selector, each with its index. Several matches are returned rather than refused — reading is not acting. Use it to check what a list, a menu or a label actually says, which is where 'undefined' shows up.

tools.name: dev_wait
tools.description: Wait for an element to appear, or with `gone` for it to leave the page. The second half is not optional: verifying that a panel closed is impossible without it.

gone.description: Wait for it to disappear instead of appear.

tools.name: dev_capture
tools.description: A picture of the unflick interface. This is the UI layer, not the decoded video: mpv draws on its own surface, which sits above the webview on Windows and below it on macOS and Linux, so no single grab means the same thing on all three. Use describe_frame for the picture itself — it comes from mpv, at higher fidelity than any compositor grab.

max_edge.description: Longest edge of the returned image in pixels. Default 768.

tools.name: dev_eval
tools.description: Run JavaScript in the unflick window and get back what it evaluated to. Either an expression or statements with an explicit `return`. The escape hatch for what the other five verbs do not cover — prefer them where they fit, because they report their own refusals in terms of the page.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for an answer. Default 5.
